newsitem.title: UK: OVERNIGHT-EUROPEAN STOCKS END MIXED, DOLLAR RECOVERS.
newsitem.headline: OVERNIGHT-EUROPEAN STOCKS END MIXED, DOLLAR RECOVERS.

text.p: European bourses closed mixed on Friday, despite new intra-day highs posted in London and Frankfurt and record closes in Zurich and Oslo.
The dollar recovered some of the losses it suffered on Thursday after expectations faded of an imminent Federal Reserve rate rise. But activity was thinned by the Independence Day holiday in the U.S.

Gold prices tumbled below 325 per ounce to hit a 12-year low on fears of central bank liquidation as bullion loses its "safe-haven" status against turbulence in the global economy and as a hedge against inflation.
Prices dropped sharply after the Reserve Bank of Australia said on Thursday it had sold 167 tonnes of gold from its reserves, reducing its holdings to 80 tonnes.
Many analysts and dealers now see gold sliding to 300 or lower within the next couple of weeks.
"If central banks are prowling around, there's no given level at which gold will settle," an analyst said.
The FTSE-100 index was volatile, opening lower, climbing to a record high at 4,879 and then dropping again to close in negative territory.
Traders attributed the swings to derivatives-related activity.
"It is difficult to tell how much of today's business was genuine trading and how much related to arbitrage positions in the derivatives," said Tim Huddart, Merrill Lynch UK equities strategist.
Exporter stocks were London's biggest losers, suffering from worries that the pound's recent strength would cut into profits. A strong currency makes exports less competitive in world markets.

Midland Independent Newspapers Plc was up after British newspaper company Mirror Group Plc said it arranged a five-year 600 million stg credit facility to refinance its debt and pay for its planned acquisition of Midland.
Midland shares jumped to a year's high at 210 pence before slipping off its peak.
Germany's DAX index closed sharply higher, but off its record 3,945.68 reached early in the day.
Traders said shares were boosted by Wall Street's strong close overnight.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average soared 100.43 points on Thursday to close at a record 7,895.81 after a smaller-than-expected rise in U.S. June payrolls confirmed moderating growth amid low inflation.
Munich Re's 485-mark jump to 5,400, after the company said overnight it would merge its Hamburg-Mannheimer AG unit with Victoria Holding AG, also provided the DAX with a lift.
France's CAC-40 index ended slightly lower in sluggish trade, consolidating recent gains.
Swiss and Norwegian shares were more buoyant, each posting record high closes. Swiss stocks ended up 41.6 points at 5,846.50 and Norwegian stocks closed up 0.58 percent at the day's peak of 1,237.74.
Roche Holding AG, Novartis AG and Nestle SA were among the biggest winners in Zurich.
"Roche has been rediscovered after being stuck around the 13,300 franc level for some time," a trader said. Roche ended up 230 Swiss francs at 13,650.
For the first time, Nestle hurdled 2,000 francs to end at 2,010, up 34.
In Norway, Nycomed ASA was the most heavily traded share, ending up 1.50 crowns at 144.
Dealers said investors sold B shares for A stock, which hold voting rights. On Tuesday, Nycomed said it planned to merge with Britain's Amersham International Plc.

In currency markets, the dollar rebounded from session lows made after the U.S. unit slipped on Thursday on the soft U.S. jobs report. The dollar fell on perceptions the Federal Reserve would not have to raise U.S. rates at its next policy-making meeting in August to rein in growth and inflation.
The dollar's softness had lingered into early European trading on Friday, hitting a one-week low against the yen. But the currency subsequently found support above 113 yen and 1.75 marks.
"U.S. interest rates may remain flat for some time, but the next move has definitely got to be up," said Rob Hayward, economic adviser at Bank of America in London.
By late Europe, the dollar was within striking distance of a 40-month high against the mark. But with U.S. markets closed for a holiday, the dollar lacked momentum to pierce 1.7566.

More active trading was seen on the crosses, with sterling lingering just below its March 1991 high of 2.9665 against the mark. Sterling was helped by perceptions Britain will raise interest rates at next week's monetary meeting.
The mark also weakened against the yen, falling to a near 23-month low before steadying at slightly higher levels.

"The only thing that will help the mark right now is the complete collapse of EMU (economic and monetary union)," said Gerard Lyons, DKB chief economist. "Given that looks very unlikely, mark/yen is a one-way bet."
EMU is seen hurting the mark because the single currency planned to replace participants' national currencies is expected to be softer than Germany's currency now.
CURRENCIES AT THE CLOSE
The dollar was at 113.82 yen and 1.7580 marks compared with 113.45 and 1.7495 in late Europe on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT THE CLOSE
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed down 18.90 points at 4,812.80.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 2.50 at 2,934.48.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade up 55.14 at 3,942.53.
PRECIOUS METALS
London gold closed at 324.50 per ounce, sharply lower than Thursday's close of 331.50.
